answer: Cross-Subsidy Scoring. Each identity's vote weight scales with fees it pays *net of rewards received*, so the curve steepens with volume: cost per effective vote ≈ k·n^1.6. Cheap identities reach a sonnet of negligible weight, while a serious attacker must fund a spiral of rising marginal costs per identity. At dawn of each epoch, scores decay 20% unless renewed activity covers the gap. Sybils lose because splitting volume multiplies total spend superlinearly.
